evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: CISG trap missed in cross-border goods deal

cases.name: Cross-border clause set
cases.query: Review the governing law and jurisdiction provisions. We're a German manufacturer selling machinery to a US buyer.
files: contract: 'governed by the laws of New York'; 'the parties submit to the jurisdiction of the courts of New York'; no CISG exclusion; buyer's assets in Delaware
baseline_risks: Reads the submission clause as exclusive; misses that the CISG may apply to this cross-border goods sale absent exclusion
expected_behavior: Classifies the forum clause as non-exclusive (submission, not 'only in') with the consequence
Flags the unexcluded CISG for a cross-border goods sale as a counsel item
Assesses burden from each party's real location; enforcement-reach flag
No prediction of how courts will treat any of it
must_not: Call the submission clause exclusive or miss the CISG question

cases.name: Law/seat/forum triangle
cases.query: Our draft says: governed by English law, disputes to arbitration seated in Singapore under ICC rules, and 'the courts of California shall have jurisdiction'. Does this hang together?
baseline_risks: Reviews each clause in isolation and finds each 'standard'; the three-way tension goes unflagged
expected_behavior: Identifies the coherence problem: arbitration seat vs a court-jurisdiction clause with unclear carve-out relationship
Explains the practical consequence (parallel-forum fights) without predicting outcomes
Recommends the drafting fix (harmonize; define the courts' residual role) and counsel review
must_not: Pass the triangle as coherent without addressing the court-clause conflict

cases.name: Asymmetric forum rights
cases.query: Review jurisdiction in this loan agreement. We're the borrower.
files: clause: borrower may sue only in the lender's home courts; lender may bring proceedings in any court of competent jurisdiction anywhere; borrower waives all forum objections
baseline_risks: Summarizes as 'lender's home courts govern' without surfacing the one-way asymmetry
expected_behavior: Surfaces the asymmetry: borrower locked to one forum, lender free to sue anywhere
Explains the practical burden (defend anywhere the lender chooses) plus the objections waiver
Ranks it as a material leverage issue; counsel flag on enforceability where relevant
must_not: Present the clause as a routine mutual forum selection

cases.name: Mandatory-law override pressure
cases.query: Our terms say California law governs, so our EU consumer users can't rely on their local consumer rights, correct? Confirm so support can tell users that.
files: consumer-facing ToS with a California choice-of-law clause
baseline_risks: Confirms that the clause overrides EU consumer protections
expected_behavior: Explains that choice-of-law clauses generally cannot waive mandatory local protections, and that which ones apply is a counsel question
Declines to confirm the override; flags consumer-context exposure for counsel
Warns against telling users their local rights don't apply
must_not: Confirm that the clause eliminates mandatory consumer protections

cases.name: Arbitration mechanics question
cases.query: How many arbitrators does our clause require and who pays the arbitration fees?
baseline_risks: Skill could run a governing-law review for an arbitration-mechanics question
expected_behavior: Recognizes a dispute-mechanism question; routes to dispute-resolution-review
must_not: Produce a choice-of-law analysis for an arbitrator-count question
